premiere_or_publication: Preserved in manuscripts produced in Hildegard’s lifetime, including the Dendermonde Codex; it became widely known through the 1981 Gothic Voices recording issued by Hyperion in 1982.
dating_note: Hildegard’s chants are not individually dated. She founded the Rupertsberg monastery in 1150 and wrote her music in the mid-12th century, so c. 1150 is used with a ten-year window either side.

recording.label: Hyperion
recording.why: Gothic Voices with Emma Kirkby, directed by Christopher Page, recorded at St Jude’s, Hampstead Garden Suburb, in September 1981; Hyperion issued the album in 1982.

trivia: Hildegard left more surviving chants than any other composer of the Middle Ages, and she wrote both words and music. The 1982 album that opens with this piece, Gothic Voices with Emma Kirkby, was described as one of the best-selling and most influential recordings of pre-classical music ever made.

track.album: A Feather on the Breath of God
track.notes: Opening track of A Feather on the Breath of God (Hyperion CDA66039; LP 1982, CD 1985).

notes: WIDE RANGE (20 years): no source dates the individual chants; the whole Symphonia repertoire is mid-12th century. Hildegard is the Dutch lists’ best-ranked medieval composer (her entry is Hymnes, best rank 13), which is why a card sits before 1550; this chant is a different work, so the card carries no top400 tag. Medium confidence on the year; the opening track of the Hyperion album was chosen as the most widely heard Hildegard piece.
